newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMG TALKING TO ANGLO ON BIGGER JCI STAKE.
newsitem.headline: AMG TALKING TO ANGLO ON BIGGER JCI STAKE.

text.p: African Mining Group (AMG) is negotiating with Anglo American Corp to buy 12.7 percent more of JCI Ltd as part of its option to gain control of South Africa's sixth-largest mining house, AMG chairman Reuel Khoza told Reuters on Tuesday.
"Negotiations for the 12.7 percent are proceeding apace," Khoza said.
He said as part of the the agreement reached with Anglo last November, AMG had the option to buy Anglo's 47.6 percent stake in JCI.

"It is not a new negotiation, we had that option all along. The transaction was about the 47.6 percent (of JCI) and pegging it at 34.9 was meant to comply with the need to certify the securities panel with regard to making an offer to minorities," he said.
Anglo spokesman Michael Spicer confirmed on Tuesday that the parties were in talks but declined to comment further.

AMG -- which groups Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd , African Renaissance Holdings and Khotso Investments among others -- agreed to buy Anglo's 34.9 percent stake for 2.88 billion rand or 54.40 rand per share.
Since then the shares fell back, although they recovered late last week and closed on Monday at 49.00 rand, the same price when the deal was struck last year.
Khoza said the 12.7 percent JCI stake was not a new tranche.
"It is not as though the 12.7 is a totally new tranche. It is part of the original arrangement," he said.
AMG has until the end of February to raise the funds to finance the purchase.
Khoza said the consortium has been talking to a number of institutions -- which he declined to name.
"We have been talking to a number of institutions. Some are positive, others don't see their way clear. And we cannot at this stage say which are which.
"But certainly there are those that have said the price is very steep -- which I believe should be pretty obvious to anybody with eyes to see and with a mind to think about the issues," he added.
Analysts have said they feared the consortium may have overpaid for the stake and have expressed worries about AMG's ability to raise the necessary funding.
But Khoza said the consortium remained positive about the deal.
"If we were not positive about managing it (JCI), we would not have made a start. But being positive does not mean you will have a 100 percent success.
"It is clearly a major transaction and I don't believe one can be categorical about a success or lack of it," he said.
